Medigap Plans.General Summary: Basic core benefits covering key hospital and medical coinsurance, but leaves deductibles to the member.
Covers Plan A's core benefits plus the Medicare Part A hospital deductible.
Near-complete coverage that includes both the Part A and Part B deductibles, leaving almost no out-of-pocket costs except Part B excess charges.
Excellent comprehensive coverage similar to Plan G, but does not cover Part B excess charges or the Part B deductible.
Historically the most popular 'first-dollar' plan. Covers 100% of all gaps, deductibles, and excess charges, leaving the member with $0 out-of-pocket costs.
Offers the exact same 100% coverage as standard Plan F, but only after the member meets a high annual deductible ($2,870 in 2026). Features very low premiums.
Medigap Plans.Foreign Travel Emergency: 80% Covered (After Deductible, up to lifetime limits)

Medigap Plans.General Summary: The gold standard for newly eligible enrollees. Covers 100% of all medical gaps, including Part B excess charges, with the single exception of the Part B annual deductible.
Offers the exact same robust coverage as standard Plan G, but only after the member meets a high annual deductible ($2,870 in 2026). Excellent option for very low monthly premiums.
Medigap Plans.Part B Deductible: 0% Covered (Not Covered - Member pays Part B deductible)
Medigap Plans.Foreign Travel Emergency: 80% Covered (After Deductible, up to lifetime limits)

Medigap Plans.General Summary: Cost-sharing plan that covers 50% of most standard Medicare gaps up to an annual out-of-pocket limit ($7,220 in 2026). Once the limit is met, the plan pays 100% of covered services.
Cost-sharing plan that covers 75% of most standard Medicare gaps up to an annual out-of-pocket limit ($3,610 in 2026). Provides a lower risk cap than Plan K.
Covers 50% of the Part A deductible and 100% of other core gaps, but excludes the Part B deductible and Part B excess charges.

Highly popular, budget-friendly plan. Covers nearly everything covered by Plan G, but requires small copays (up to $20 for office visits, up to $50 for emergency room visits) and does not cover Part B excess charges.
Medigap Plans.Part B Coinsurance: 100% Covered (Except copays up to $20/office visit and $50/ER visit)
Medigap Plans.Part B Excess Charges: 0% Covered (Not Covered - Medical providers can bill up to 15% above Medicare rate)

Medigap Carriers.Key Characteristics: Co-branded with AARP. Offers stable pricing, household discounts in most states, and a highly recognized national network.
Renowned for competitive rates, excellent senior customer service, and solid household premium discounts.
Highly trusted local brand recognition. Plan options and pricing models are managed independently by state affiliates.
Offers strong financial stability and competitive rates in many markets, with extra member wellness discounts.
Provides highly competitive premiums in several states, 24/7 health information lines, and digital customer support tools.
Strong customer service orientation, very competitive rates in southern states, and additional value-add programs.
Fastest-growing Medigap portfolio. Offers multi-policy discounts and flexible underwriting options.

Advantage Plan Types.Description: Standard managed care network. Requires choosing a Primary Care Physician (PCP) and obtaining official referrals to see specialists. Out-of-network care is not covered except in emergencies.
Advantage Plan Types.Pros / Advantages: Lowest monthly premiums (often $0), low copays, frequently bundles robust extra benefits (dental, vision, gym).
Advantage Plan Types.Cons / Trade-offs: Strict provider lock-in, referral administration friction, high prior authorization frequency.

Advantage Plan Types.Description: Provides more network flexibility. Members can see out-of-network providers (at a higher copay/coinsurance rate) and do not need a PCP referral to see specialists.
Advantage Plan Types.Pros / Advantages: Freedom to see specialists without referrals, out-of-network emergency and non-emergency coverage.
Advantage Plan Types.Cons / Trade-offs: Slightly higher monthly premiums than HMOs, higher out-of-pocket costs for out-of-network care, still subject to prior authorizations.

Advantage Plan Types.Description: An HMO plan hybrid that permits members to use certain out-of-network medical services for a higher out-of-pocket cost.
Advantage Plan Types.Pros / Advantages: Keeps the low cost of an HMO while adding a safety valve for specific out-of-network specialists.
Advantage Plan Types.Cons / Trade-offs: POS benefits may be capped, and prior authorizations are still tightly enforced.

Advantage Plan Types.Description: A plan that determines how much it will pay providers and how much the member pays. Providers must agree to accept the plan's terms of payment on a patient-by-patient basis.
Advantage Plan Types.Pros / Advantages: Extremely flexible network *if* the physician accepts the plan's terms.
Advantage Plan Types.Cons / Trade-offs: Very few providers accept PFFS terms anymore; high risk of being turned away at the doctor's office.

Advantage Plan Types.Description: A highly specialized plan designed to coordinate benefits, copays, and care for individuals who are low-income or disabled and qualify for both government systems.
Advantage Plan Types.Pros / Advantages: $0 premiums, $0 medical copays, massive OTC pharmacy allowances, comprehensive care coordinators.
Advantage Plan Types.Cons / Trade-offs: Restricted network and strict eligibility verification.

Advantage Plan Types.Description: Tailors plan benefits, provider networks, and drug formularies specifically to help members manage their long-term chronic medical conditions.
Advantage Plan Types.Pros / Advantages: Networks include dedicated disease specialists, highly optimized drug formularies for specialized medications, targeted care management.
Advantage Plan Types.Cons / Trade-offs: Requires recurring medical verification; narrow provider network outside of the specialized disease area.

Advantage Plan Types.Description: Combines a high-deductible health plan with a bank savings account. Medicare deposits funds directly into the account for the member to spend on healthcare.
Advantage Plan Types.Pros / Advantages: Total freedom of provider choice (any doctor who accepts Medicare), no network locking, funds roll over year-to-year.
Advantage Plan Types.Cons / Trade-offs: Does not cover prescription drugs (member must buy a standalone Part D plan); high out-of-pocket deductible risk if severe health events occur.

Advantage Carriers.Network Strength: Very High (Massive national HMO and PPO networks)
Advantage Carriers.Key Characteristics: Industry leader. Integrates broad clinical partnerships, OTC allowances, and comprehensive renew rewards programs.

Advantage Carriers.Network Strength: High (Highly focused on senior networks and primary care centers)
Advantage Carriers.Key Characteristics: Consistently rated highest in customer satisfaction. Strong regional HMO options and specialized care programs.

Advantage Carriers.Network Strength: High (Integrates CVS Pharmacy, MinuteClinic, and medical providers)
Advantage Carriers.Key Characteristics: Leverages CVS locations for convenient member health screenings and benefits integration, offering competitive zero-dollar premiums.

Advantage Carriers.Network Strength: Strong (Uses local Blue Cross Blue Shield provider networks)
Advantage Carriers.Key Characteristics: Offers trusted Blue Cross branding with excellent regional coverage and solid dental and vision supplementary benefits.

Advantage Carriers.Network Strength: Moderate (Very focused on low-cost options and Special Needs Plans)
Advantage Carriers.Key Characteristics: Known for highly competitive Part B premium give-back plans and extensive D-SNP Medicaid coordination options.
Operates as a highly coordinated one-stop-shop. Exceptional care coordination, but members are locked exclusively to Kaiser facilities.

Advantage Carriers.Network Strength: Moderate (Good urban PPO and HMO networks)
Advantage Carriers.Key Characteristics: Offers a strong suite of customer incentives and solid dental coverage add-ons in key metropolitan areas.
A highly modern, tech-enabled startup-style carrier. Excellent customer loyalty ratings and individualized member care guides.
Specializes deeply in dual-eligible (D-SNP) populations, aligning state Medicaid benefits with federal Medicare benefits.

Part D Rx Plans.Best Suited For: Seniors taking no regular medications, or taking only common, low-cost generic drugs.
Part D Rx Plans.Key Features & Benefits: Low premiums, standard deductible, very low tier-1 copays at preferred pharmacies.

Part D Rx Plans.Best Suited For: Seniors taking a mix of generic maintenance medications and one or two brand-name prescriptions.
Part D Rx Plans.Key Features & Benefits: Balanced formulary coverage, moderate deductible, broad network of preferred retail pharmacies.

Part D Rx Plans.Best Suited For: Seniors with complex medication regimens requiring specialized, high-tier brand-name drugs.
Part D Rx Plans.Key Features & Benefits: Often features $0 deductibles on Tier 1 and Tier 2 drugs, comprehensive formulary coverages, and reduced coinsurance rates on specialty drugs.

Part D Carriers.Key Characteristics & Strengths: Often offers the lowest base premiums in the nation. Excellent integration with CVS mail-order and retail pharmacies.

Part D Carriers.Market Share / Coverage Tier: Dominant (Co-branded with Value Script and Classic plans)
Part D Carriers.Key Characteristics & Strengths: Highly competitive low-cost plans. Popular option for seniors who only take generic medications and want a near-$0 premium.
Outstanding pharmacy network. Offers extremely reliable formulary updates and highly predictable co-pay structures.
Straightforward plan options with highly responsive customer service and easy enrollment processes.

Part D Carriers.Market Share / Coverage Tier: High (Partners with Walmart Rx plans in many states)
Part D Carriers.Key Characteristics & Strengths: Very popular budget option due to strong retail partnerships, offering discounted copays at Walmart and Humana mail-order pharmacies.
Well-balanced plan selections featuring high-tier coverage options suitable for brand-name drug requirements.
